[anti-pattern] [warning] "packages/rex/src/public.ts" is production code imported only by tests (8 importer(s), all test files) — either it is dead or its real caller is missing
[anti-pattern] [warning] warning: Engine-to-feature back edges. About 26 imports from the store/schema/analyze layer reach into migrations/ or recommend/. Shared types those callers need (for example the recommend/types.ts shapes) should move down into schema/ so the dependency runs one way only.
[pattern] [info] info: migrations/registry.ts is a clean extension seam. Its header says one entry per migration folder and nothing reads it except the migrate command, so adding or removing a migration touches one file.
[pattern] [info] info: migration-plan-data.ts says it is pure and deterministic, keyed by v1 item id, and never shells out. Outside facts are injected by the caller. This keeps the migration plan replayable, so new code in this folder should keep that boundary.

</findings>

<insights>

- 133 entry points — wide API surface, consider consolidating exports
- Zones "Rex" and "Rex Cli" may be one architectural concept; the import graph links them but the judgment was undecided.
- Zone "rex" has files across 6 directories — consider consolidating under a dedicated directory
- "packages/rex/src/public.ts" is production code imported only by tests (8 importer(s), all test files) — either it is dead or its real caller is missing
- [call graph] 154 internal calls, 27 outgoing, 315 incoming (cohesion: 0.85, coupling: 0.15)
- The zone names look swapped. The 181 rex → rex-cli edges show this 15-file zone (migrations, recommend, codeowners, workflow, public.ts) sitting on top of the engine: store, schema, core and analyze, which Louvain put in "rex-cli". Read the 26 reverse edges as engine code reaching up into feature modules. They are not a CLI depending on its library.
- public.ts is the package entry that other packages use through their gateways (hench src/prd/rex-gateway.ts, web src/server/rex-gateway.ts). The "imported only by tests" result most likely comes from the graph not resolving bare `@n-dx/rex` specifiers to this file, so it is a gap in import resolution and does not mean the code is dead.
- The zone has no single theme. Migration v1→v2, recommendation similarity/conflict detection, CODEOWNERS generation and the default workflow types share no domain concept. They cluster because they all use the same store/schema types.

</insights>
